places.title: Ciutat Vella
places.why: The old walled city inside the ring of boulevards that replaced its ramparts: a dense maze of medieval lanes, Gothic churches, Baroque palaces and small squares. In its north-west corner, El Carme is the bohemian quarter of bars, street art and crumbling townhouses.
places.note: The district boundary follows the line of the 14th-century wall; the protected historic ensemble extends beyond it into the 19th-century Eixample.

places.title: Catedral de València, the Micalet and Plaça de la Mare de Déu
places.architect: Andreu Julià and others (Micalet); Conrad Rudolf (Baroque portal); Diego Martínez Ponce de Urrana (Basilica)
places.why: A cathedral raised over the great mosque, with three portals in three styles: Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque. The octagonal Gothic bell tower, the Micalet, gives the best view over the old town; beside it, Plaça de la Mare de Déu with the domed Basilica of the Virgin occupies the site of the Roman forum.

places.title: Llotja de la Seda
places.why: The silk and commodity exchange of Valencia’s golden century, a masterpiece of late Gothic civil architecture. In the trading hall, twisted columns rise into palm-like ribbed vaults 17 metres above the floor; next door are the tower, the Consulate of the Sea and a courtyard of orange trees.

photos.author: Juan Mayordomo

places.title: Mercat Central
places.architect: Alejandro Soler March, Francisco Guardia Vial
places.why: One of Europe’s largest covered food markets, still run by local traders: a modernista hall of iron, glass and ceramic tiles under two domes crowned by a parrot and a swordfish. It faces the Llotja across the square.

photos.file: 056 Mercat Central de València, accés est, pl. del Mercat.jpg

photos.author: Michielverbeek

places.title: Ciutat de les Arts i les Ciències
places.why: Calatrava’s white skeletal buildings in the dry bed of the Turia: a planetarium shaped like an eye, a science museum ribbed like a whale, an opera house under a crest of steel, all set in shallow pools. At the far end, the thin concrete shells of the Oceanogràfic were Félix Candela’s last design.

points.name: Palau de les Arts Reina Sofia

photos.file: Palau de Les Arts Reina Sofía - Pool View - City of Arts and Sciences - Valencia Spain.jpg
photos.author: MCAE Consulting

places.title: Jardí del Túria
places.architect: Ricardo Bofill, Vetges Tu i Mediterrània and others
places.why: After the flood of 1957 the river was diverted south, and its dry bed became a nine-kilometre ribbon of parkland crossed by eighteen bridges, from medieval arches to Calatrava. Locals cycle, run and picnic here; the giant Gulliver playground lies near the Palau de la Música.

photos.author: Dorieo

places.title: Torres de Serrans and Torres de Quart
places.architect: Pere Balaguer (Serrans); Pere Bonfill, Francesc Baldomar and Pere Compte (Quart)
places.why: The two surviving gates of the medieval wall. Serrans is a monumental Gothic entrance facing the riverbed; Quart, built half a century later, still bears cannonball scars from the siege of 1808. Both can be climbed for views over the rooftops.

places.title: Plaça de l’Ajuntament
places.architect: Javier Goerlich (square); Carlos Carbonell and Francisco Mora (Town Hall); Miguel Ángel Navarro (Post Office); Cayetano Borso di Carminati (Rialto)
places.why: The civic heart of the city, a vast triangle framed by early 20th-century facades: the Town Hall, the Post Office with its glass dome, the classical Ateneo and the rationalist Rialto cinema. Pedestrianised in the 2020s, it is now a place to walk rather than drive.

photos.author: Enric

places.title: Estació del Nord
places.why: A railway terminus that celebrates the orange trade: ceramic oranges and blossoms decorate the facade, and the ticket hall is lined with mosaics, glazed tiles and carved wood, with wishes of a good journey written in several languages.

photos.file: Estación del Norte, Valencia, España, 2014-06-30, DD 122.JPG
photos.author: Diego Delso

places.title: Mercat de Colón
places.why: A modernista market hall with brick and ceramic arches, iron and glass, restored in 2003 as a covered square of cafés, horchata bars and restaurants in the heart of the Eixample.

photos.file: Valencia-l'Eixample, Mercado de Colon RI-51-0008310 IMG 2715 2026-08-23 14.06.jpg
photos.author: Michielverbeek

places.title: El Cabanyal
places.why: The old fishermen’s quarter by the beach: long parallel streets that follow the rows of former reed huts, lined with low houses clad in colourful tiles. Saved after years of opposition to a plan to cut an avenue through it, it now mixes old taverns with new cafés.

places.title: Platja de la Malva-rosa and the Passeig Marítim
places.why: A wide seafront promenade behind a broad sandy beach, from the Neptú rice restaurants past Les Arenes to the Malva-rosa, where the novelist Blasco Ibáñez had his summer house. The city’s evening walk by the sea.

places.title: L’Albufera
places.why: A shallow freshwater lagoon ringed by rice fields and pine-covered dunes just south of the city. Boats go out at sunset from El Palmar, the village of paella; along the sea, the Devesa’s dunes were rebuilt in the 1980s and 90s after a resort plan was halted.

photos.file: Marjal Sud. Casa dels Catalans i solcs 2.JPG
photos.author: Enrique Íñiguez Rodríguez ( Qoan )

places.title: Russafa
places.why: A grid of late 19th-century apartment blocks south of the station, now the city’s liveliest quarter for cafés, galleries and small shops. Its market is a bold concrete hall of the 1950s by Julio Bellot.

places.title: Jardí Botànic de la Universitat de València
places.why: One of Europe’s oldest university botanic gardens, on its present site since 1802: palms, cacti and old trees in themed beds, a 19th-century iron shade house and greenhouses, all within walls a few steps from the Torres de Quart.

photos.file: Umbracle del Jardí Botànic de València zinc.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Jardins del Real (Vivers)
places.why: The grounds of the vanished palace of Valencia’s kings, demolished in 1810, now a large public garden with rose beds, fountains, statues and an avenue of old trees beside the Turia.

photos.file: Rosaleda de los Jardines del Real, Valencia 03.jpg
photos.author: 19Tarrestnom65

photos.file: Arbres als jardins de Vivers de València.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Jardí de Monforte
places.why: A romantic 19th-century garden around a small palace: clipped myrtle hedges, marble statues and fountains, laid out by Sebastián Monleón. Small, walled and quiet.

places.title: Parc Central
places.why: A new park on the old railway land south of the Estació del Nord: terraced gardens, water features, playgrounds and restored brick train sheds now used as halls for culture and sport. It stitches together districts long divided by the tracks.

places.title: Parc de Capçalera
places.why: At the western head of the Turia garden, a park that recreates the river’s lost landscape: a boating lake, low hills with views, Mediterranean planting and riverside trees.

places.title: Jardí de les Hespèrides
places.why: A small walled garden next to the Botanic Garden that retells the myth of the golden apples and revives the Renaissance Valencian taste for ornamental citrus: rows of orange and lemon trees, cypress hedges, a pool and sculptures of Hercules, the nymphs and the dragon.

photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Palauet i Jardí d’Aiora
places.why: An eclectic late 19th-century summer villa with modernista details, set in a public garden of palms and old trees in the Aiora district.

places.title: La Glorieta and El Parterre
places.why: Two small 19th-century gardens by the Porta de la Mar, shaded by enormous ficus trees. The Parterre holds the equestrian statue of King Jaume I, the conqueror of Valencia.

places.title: Passeig de l’Albereda
places.why: The city’s historic promenade across the river from the old town: a long walk of palms, plane trees and fountains between the Jardins del Real and Calatrava’s Exposició bridge.

photos.file: Estatuas de Juan Méjica en la Alameda de Valencia 04.jpg
photos.author: 19Tarrestnom65

places.title: Parc de Marxalenes
places.why: An eight-hectare neighbourhood park north of the Turia, won by residents who campaigned to keep the land green. Old farmhouses such as the Alqueria de Barrinto survive among its tree-lined walks, lawns and shaded tables.

photos.author: Enric

places.title: Jardí de l’Antic Hospital
places.why: The garden left by the demolition in 1974 of the 15th-century Hospital dels Innocents, redesigned by Guillermo Vázquez Consuegra: stepped earth paths, trees and scattered archaeological stones around the surviving infirmary, now the public library, and the chapel of Santa Llúcia.

photos.file: Roses al jardí de l'hospital de València.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: Parc de l'antic hospital general de València.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Finca Roja
places.why: A whole city block of 378 working-class flats in red brick, inspired by Dutch expressionism: round corner towers, green ceramic trim and bay windows around a large inner courtyard reached through passages from the street.

photos.file: Pati de la Finca Roja de València, bardissa.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Edifici Santa Maria Micaela
places.why: A cooperative block of 138 duplex flats with an exposed concrete frame and brick infill, a raised walkway under a pergola and a shared garden with a pool at ground level — Valencia’s answer to Le Corbusier’s Unité.

photos.file: Edifici Santa Maria Micaela de València, façana.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: Edifici Santa Maria Micaela Grup Residencial Agents Comercials, València.jpg
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Torre Solar, Sociópolis
places.why: A tower of 124 social housing flats in the Sociópolis district, on the edge of the southern huerta. Every flat has two orientations for cross-ventilation, and the top floors break up into a crown of terraces.

places.title: Casa dels Dracs
places.why: A corner apartment house covered in fantastic neo-Gothic stonework: dragons, gargoyles and winged creatures crawl over the balconies and the corner.

photos.file: Casa de los Dragones en Valencia.jpg
photos.author: Juan Mayordomo

places.title: Casa Ortega
places.why: A modernista apartment house on the Gran Via with a richly sculpted stone facade, floral reliefs and figures framing the balconies.

photos.file: Balcó i atlants, Casa Ortega de València.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: Part superior de la porta de la casa Ortega, València.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Edifici Chapa
places.architect: Antonio Martorell, Emilio Ferrer, Carlos Carbonell
places.why: A single modernista apartment block with a facade almost 200 metres long, wrapping the Gran Via corner and the oval of Plaça de Cánovas in five even storeys of ornate balconies.

places.title: Casa Ordeig
places.why: A modernista apartment house on the corner of the market square and Carrer dels Ramilletes, by Francisco Mora, the architect of the Mercat de Colón.

photos.file: Torre de la casa Ordeig de València.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Veles e Vents
places.architect: David Chipperfield Architects, b720 Fermín Vázquez Arquitectos
places.why: Built in eleven months for the America’s Cup: four white horizontal decks that cantilever far out over each other, giving deep shade to the terraces and open views over the old port and the beaches. The heart of the regenerated Marina.

photos.file: Veles e vents from Alinghi's base (488076076).jpg
photos.author: Visentico / Sento

places.title: Palau de Congressos
places.why: Foster’s convention centre is shaped like an eye: two long curved facades meet at the ends under a vast overhanging roof that shades the glass from the Mediterranean sun.

photos.file: Palau de Congressos de València, País Valencià.jpg
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: Façana est del palau de congressos, València.jpg
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: MuVIM — Museu Valencià de la Il·lustració i de la Modernitat
places.why: A museum of concrete and glass that folds and cuts itself to fit a tight corner beside the old Beneficència, with sharp overhangs, set in a small garden.

photos.file: Museu Valencià de la Il·lustració i de la Modernitat, València, País Valencià.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: IVAM — Institut Valencià d’Art Modern
places.why: Spain’s first museum of modern art, opened in 1989 on the edge of El Carme. In the basement, a stretch of the medieval city wall runs through the Sala de la Muralla.

places.title: Museu de Belles Arts (Col·legi de Sant Pius V)
places.why: A Baroque seminary college with a blue-tiled dome across the river from the old town, now one of Spain’s great picture galleries, strong in Gothic Valencian altarpieces, Sorolla and a self-portrait by Velázquez.

photos.file: Museo de las Bellas Artes de Valencia - St. Pius VI Palace - Valencia Spain.jpg
photos.author: MCAE Consulting

photos.file: Museo de Belas Artes de Valencia 02.jpg
photos.author: Bene Riobó

places.title: Palau del Marqués de Dosaigües
places.why: A Gothic mansion remade in the Rococo: its extravagant alabaster portal shows two river gods pouring water, around a Virgin of the Rosary. Inside, the National Ceramics Museum and ornate 19th-century salons.

photos.file: Valencia, palazzo de marchese di Dos Aigües, esterno 01.jpg
photos.author: Francesco Bini
Nan Palmero from San Antonio, TX, USA

photos.file: Valencia - Palacio del Marqués de Dos Aguas - Salón Rojo 2026-05-16 03.jpg
photos.author: Rafa Esteve

places.title: Centre d’Art Hortensia Herrero (Palau de Valeriola)
places.why: A palace of medieval origin on Carrer del Mar restored as a contemporary art centre: Roman remains in the basement, the old courtyards opened up and new pieces set into the historic rooms.

places.title: Bombas Gens
places.architect: Cayetano Borso di Carminati; Ramón Esteve, Eduardo de Miguel, Annabelle Selldorf
places.why: An Art Deco factory for hydraulic pumps whose street front hides the sheds behind curving walls and stylised plant motifs. Restored in 2017 as an art centre, with brick and galvanised steel for the new parts.

photos.file: Edificio Bombas Gens Centro de Arte 19.jpg
photos.author: 19Tarrestnom65

photos.file: Edificio Bombas Gens Centro de Arte 14.jpg
photos.author: 19Tarrestnom65

places.title: Palau de la Música
places.architect: José María García de Paredes; Eduardo de Miguel (extension)
places.why: A concert hall in the Turia garden fronted by a long glass vault that runs parallel to the old riverbed; the lobby is a winter garden, and a pool designed by Ricardo Bofill stretches in front.

photos.file: Palau de la Música de València i font.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: Palau de la Música de València, vista lateral.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Teatre El Musical
places.why: A theatre and civic centre in the Cabanyal that keeps the neoclassical front of the old Ateneu Musical: behind it, a 400-seat hall fits a plot hemmed in by neighbours, and the foyer is lit from above through a veil of timber slats.

photos.file: Teatre El Musical i església del Rosari.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Església de Sant Nicolau
places.why: A plain Gothic church hidden behind a lane, whose single nave is covered entirely by Baroque frescoes after designs by Antonio Palomino. Restored in 2016, it is nicknamed the Valencian Sistine Chapel.

photos.file: Chiesa di san Nicola e san pietro martire Valencia (3).jpg
photos.author: Elisa Marianini

photos.file: Església de Sant Nicolau de València, rosassa i campanar.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Plaça Redona
places.why: A perfectly circular little square enclosed by a ring of houses, laid out in 1840 as a market, with a fountain in the middle and small craft and haberdashery stalls.

places.title: Església dels Sants Joans
places.why: A Gothic church facing the Mercat Central, dressed in Baroque: a facade to the market with a clock and statues, and inside a vault frescoed by Antonio Palomino, recovered after the fire of 1936.

photos.file: Sant Joan del Mercat Valencia Marcok f17.jpg
photos.author: Marcok

photos.file: Valencia - Iglesia de los Santos Juanes - 2026-08-26 04.jpg
photos.author: Rafa Esteve

places.title: Església de Santa Caterina
places.why: A Gothic church with an ambulatory, best known for its slender hexagonal Baroque bell tower, which closes the view along Carrer de la Pau.

photos.file: Iglesia de Santa Catarina, Valencia, España, 2014-06-30, DD 143.jpg
photos.author: Diego Delso

places.title: Sant Joan de l’Hospital
places.why: The oldest church in the city, founded by the Knights Hospitaller after the conquest of 1238: a sober single nave behind a courtyard of ceramic panels, with a medieval cemetery and the remains of the Roman circus beneath.

photos.file: Capela do cemiterio de de Sant Joan de l'Hospital.jpg
photos.author: Bene Riobó

photos.file: Valencia - Iglesia de San Juan del Hospital 01.jpg
photos.author: Zarateman

photos.file: Arcosolios do cemiterio de de Sant Joan de l'Hospital.jpg
photos.author: Bene Riobó

places.title: Palau de la Generalitat
places.why: The Gothic palace of the Generalitat of the old kingdom of Valencia, extended in the Renaissance with a tower and halls under richly carved and gilded wooden ceilings.

photos.file: 043 Palau de la Generalitat Valenciana, angle nord-oest, pl. de Manises.jpg
photos.author: Enric

photos.file: Palau de la Generalitat Valenciana - Valencia - 20200810 003.jpg
photos.author: Américo Toledano

places.title: Real Col·legi del Corpus Christi (el Patriarca)
places.why: A Counter-Reformation seminary founded by Archbishop Juan de Ribera, around one of the finest Renaissance cloisters in Spain, with a double tier of marble columns.

places.title: Monestir de Sant Miquel dels Reis
places.architect: Alonso de Covarrubias, Juan de Vidanya and others
places.why: A Renaissance monastery of the Hieronymites founded by the Duke of Calabria, often cited as a forerunner of El Escorial. Long used as a prison, it now houses the Valencian Library around its two cloisters.

photos.file: Valencia - Monasterio de San Miguel de los Reyes 05 2017-05-01.jpg
photos.author: Rafa Esteve

photos.file: Monestir de Sant Miquel dels Reis Monasterio de San Miguel de los Reyes.jpg
photos.author: Sento

photos.file: Monasterio de San Miguel de los Reyes 17.jpg
photos.author: Jerónimo Roure

photos.file: València. Sant Miquel dels Reis. Església. Portada.jpg

places.title: Almodí
places.why: The medieval grain exchange: a tall hall around a covered courtyard, its walls painted with popular religious scenes of the 17th and 18th centuries.

photos.file: 203 L'Almodí (València), façana est, pl. Sant Lluís Bertran.jpg
photos.author: Enric

places.title: Banys de l’Almirall
places.why: Public steam baths built in Christian times on the Islamic model: small vaulted rooms lit by star-shaped openings in the ceiling, in use until the 20th century.

places.title: Centre del Carme
places.why: A Carmelite convent turned into a centre for contemporary culture: a Gothic cloister and a Renaissance one, a chapter house and long galleries, open to walk through for free.

photos.file: Valencia - Reial Monestir de Nostra Senyora del Carme (Centre del Carme) 01.jpg
photos.author: Zarateman

photos.file: Façana del Carme abans de la seua restauració.jpg
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: Exterior de la Iglesia de la Santa Cruz, Valencia 01.jpg
photos.author: 19Tarrestnom65

places.title: Palau de l’Exposició
places.why: A neo-Gothic and modernista pavilion built for the 1909 Regional Exhibition, with Nolla mosaic floors and large stained-glass windows.

photos.file: Biblioteca Municipal Palau de l'Exposicio - panoramio.jpg
photos.author: Mister No

places.title: Casa del Punt de Gantxo
places.why: A modernista apartment house on Plaça de l’Almoina whose facade is covered in floral reliefs so dense they look like crochet lace, with wrought-iron balconies.

photos.file: Casa del Punt de Ganxo, València, Espanya - panoramio retouched.jpg
photos.author: Mister No

photos.file: 303 Casa del Punt de Ganxo (València), plaça de l'Almoina.jpg
photos.author: Enric

places.title: Edifici del Banc de València
places.why: A monumental bank on a triangular corner plot, begun by Almenar and finished by Goerlich, whose rounded prow recalls New York’s Flatiron.

photos.file: Banco de Valencia, Valencia, España, 2014-06-30, DD 134.JPG
photos.author: Diego Delso

photos.file: Intersection at Banco de Valencia, Ciutat Vella, Valencia, Spain, 2024 January.jpg
photos.author: Ximonic (Simo Räsänen)

places.title: Casa Niederleytner (Palacio Santa Clara)
places.why: An elegant bourgeois apartment house on a corner of the Eixample, an early work of Javier Goerlich, now a hotel that keeps its facade and staircase.

places.title: Tinglados and Edifici del Rellotge
places.why: The old port’s modernista warehouses, with iron roofs and ceramic panels of oranges and fruit from the huerta, and the clock tower building that marks the entrance to the harbour.

photos.file: Tinglado nº 2 del Puerto de Valencia 02.jpg
photos.author: Dorieo

photos.file: Sede de la autoridad portuaria de Valencia.JPG
photos.author: M4n0locervera

photos.file: Detall del fris del cobert n. 2 del port de València.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: Torre del rellotge, port de València.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Drassanes del Grau
places.why: Medieval shipyards by the old port: a row of long parallel Gothic halls with pointed diaphragm arches, where galleys were built and stored.

photos.file: Exterior de les drassanes del Grau.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: València, arc de diafragma de les drassanes.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Plaça de Bous
places.why: A neoclassical bullring beside the Estació del Nord, modelled on Roman amphitheatres: tiers of brick arcades wrapping the ring.

photos.file: Plaza de toros, Valencia, España, 2014-06-30, DD 126.JPG
photos.author: Diego Delso

photos.file: Plaza de Toros de Valencia - Columns and Arches.jpg
photos.author: MCAE Consulting

places.title: Palau de Justícia
places.why: Charles III’s royal customs house, a palace of brick and stone with a balustraded cornice and sculpture, later a tobacco factory and now the regional high court.

places.title: Església i Palau del Temple
places.why: The neoclassical church and palace of the Order of Montesa, built on the site of the Templars’ house by the old city wall.

photos.file: Iglesia y Palacio del Temple - Ciutat Vella, Valencia, Spain.jpg
photos.author: MCAE Consulting

photos.file: Iglesia y Palacio del Temple - Upper Towers and Pediment - Valencia Spain.jpg
photos.author: MCAE Consulting

places.title: Reial Monestir de la Trinitat
places.why: A convent of Poor Clares across the Turia with one of the most beautiful Gothic cloisters in the city and the tomb of Queen Maria of Castile.

photos.file: Real Monasterio de la Santísima Trinidad - Valencia Spain.jpg
photos.author: MCAE Consulting

places.title: Església de les Escoles Pies
places.why: A circular neoclassical church whose dome is one of the largest in Spain; its restoration was recognised in the 2025 regional architecture awards.

photos.file: Cúpula capilla de las Escuelas pías de la calle Carniceros de Valencia 02.jpg
photos.author: 19Tarrestnom65

places.title: Pont de l’Exposició and Alameda station
places.why: A leaning steel arch by Calatrava, nicknamed la Peineta, over the Turia garden, with a metro station beneath: white ribbed concrete vaults lit through glass blocks set in the square above.

photos.file: Puente de la Exposición, Valencia - panoramio.jpg
photos.author: Carlos Cunha

places.title: Fira València
places.architect: José María Tomás Llavador (extension and Events Centre)
places.why: The trade fair grounds by the metro to Benimàmet: 1969 exhibition pavilions from the modern movement, and a vast extension whose Events Centre sits under a pointed glass vault.
places.note: Open during trade fairs; the buildings are seen from the street at other times.

photos.file: Feria Valencia - Fira de València - Valencia Trade Fair place 04.jpg
photos.author: Punteador

photos.file: Feria Valencia - Fira de València - Valencia Trade Fair place 02.jpg
photos.author: Punteador

places.title: Biblioteca Gregori Maians
places.why: Giorgio Grassi’s library for the Tarongers campus: a long, severe brick building in his rationalist manner, a counterpoint to the new university district around it.

photos.file: Universitat de València, façana de la biblioteca de Ciències Socials Gregori Maians.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: Biblioteca de Ciències Socials Gregori Maians 09.jpg
photos.author: 19Tarrestnom65

photos.file: Biblioteca de Ciències Socials Gregori Maians 01.jpg
photos.author: 19Tarrestnom65

places.title: Teatre Romà de Sagunt
places.why: A Roman theatre cut into the castle hill, controversially rebuilt in the 1990s: new brick walls reconstruct the stage building so that plays can again be performed.
places.note: In Sagunt, 25 km north; about 30 minutes by Cercanías train.

photos.file: Teatro romano por la parte de atrás.jpg
photos.author: 19Tarrestnom65

places.title: Col·legi Alemany
places.why: A school designed by the German federal building office and completed in 1961: Bauhaus-inspired pavilions of glass and brick around gardens, with Nolla ceramic tiles on the front.
places.note: A working school; seen from the street.

places.title: Palau del Marqués de Campo
places.why: The palace of the 19th-century banker and mayor José Campo, with a restrained facade on Plaça de l’Arquebisbe; it now houses the City Museum around its courtyard.

photos.file: 290 Palau del Marquès de Campo, Museu de la Ciutat (València), pati.jpg
photos.author: Enric

photos.file: 263 Palau del Marquès de Campo, Museu de la Ciutat (València), una de les sales.jpg
photos.author: Enric

places.title: Col·legi de l’Art Major de la Seda
places.why: The guild hall of the silk weavers since 1494, rebuilt in the Baroque with 18th-century ceramic floors; it tells the story of the industry that made Valencia rich.

photos.file: Colegio del Arte Mayor de la Seda, Valencia 02.jpg
photos.author: Dorieo

photos.file: Colegio del Arte Mayor de la Seda, Valencia 01.jpg
photos.author: Dorieo

photos.file: Colegio del Arte Mayor de la Seda, Valencia 03.jpg
photos.author: Dorieo

places.title: Espai Verd
places.why: A cooperative housing megastructure on the edge of the huerta: 108 homes stacked like terraced houses in the air, with hanging gardens, trees and pools on every level of the concrete frame.

photos.file: Part superior de l'edifici d'habitatges Espai Verd, València.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: Carrer i edifici Espai Verd, Benimaclet.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: Edifici Espai Verd de València, exterior.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: University faculties by Fernando Moreno Barberá
places.why: Three faculties along the Avinguda de Blasco Ibáñez that brought Mies and Le Corbusier to Valencia: glass curtain walls beside concrete brise-soleils, full-height lobbies with murals, garden courtyards and, at the School of Agronomy, two steel staircases hung from the structure.

points.name: Former Faculty of Law (Philosophy and Education)
Former Faculty of Arts (Geography and History)

photos.file: Facultat de Filosofia de la Universitat de València, lateral.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: Facultat de Geografia i Història de la Universitat de València.jpg
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Torre de Ripalda (La Pagoda)
places.architect: Antonio Escario, José Vives, José Antonio Vidal
places.why: A luxury apartment tower facing the Jardins del Real, stepped back in two wings with balconies that curl up at the corners like the eaves of a Japanese pagoda.

places.title: Casa Judía
places.why: An Art Deco apartment house dressed as an Egyptian and oriental fantasy, with coloured reliefs, stepped cornices and a Star of David by the entrance.

photos.file: Llinda sobre la porta de la casa Jueva de València.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: La Rambleta
places.why: A tall grey box of a cultural centre on the southern outskirts, its long sides clad in hinged window panels, set on the edge of a neighbourhood park with a lagoon, a small stream and a riverside wood.

photos.file: Panells de les finestres de l'espai Rambleta, València.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

photos.file: Llacuna del parc de la Rambleta i l'espai Rambleta.JPG
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Parròquia de Jesús Mestre
places.architect: José Antonio Corrales, Ramón Vázquez Molezún
places.why: A church of the Second Vatican Council in Madrid-style exposed brick: one open space for the congregation around an advanced altar, a tall light-filled volume over the sanctuary like a dome, and a long band of stained glass along the side.

places.title: Institut Sorolla
places.why: A secondary school of 1960s concrete bravura by José Ramón Azpiazu: umbrella shells in the manner of Félix Candela, folded-plate roofs and huge cantilevered beams over a stepped plan of courtyards.
places.note: A working school; seen from the street.

photos.file: Voladís de l'institut Sorolla de València.jpg
photos.author: Joanbanjo

places.title: Col·legi Pureza de María
places.why: A school and convent: a long, disciplined block of classrooms with the nuns’ residence set back on the roof, and beside it a church with a jagged, expressive outline.
places.note: A working school; seen from the street.

photos.file: Colegio Pureza de María de Valencia 07.jpg
photos.author: 19Tarrestnom65

photos.file: Colegio Pureza de María de Valencia 06.jpg
photos.author: 19Tarrestnom65

photos.file: Colegio Pureza de María de Valencia 01.jpg
photos.author: 19Tarrestnom65

places.title: Col·legi Guadalaviar
places.why: A school scattered as low pavilions among gardens, with an intimate scale and constant views between classrooms and courtyards; the tallest block was fitted with adjustable metal louvres, bold for its time.
places.note: A working school; seen from the street.
